title: Choose the dashboard's new visual world
question: The roll assigned Field Atlas. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Field Atlas
options.lineage: University botanical field guides and specimen plates
options.thesis: Read one living plant as a clear chain from measured soil to forecast to pump.
options.viewport: A compact live header leads to a five-step state rail; the center gives the moisture trace and two large readings, while a right column holds decision and the manual burst. Firmware safety, model quality, and data provenance anchor the bottom. A measured leaf-vein marker reacts to each new reading without replacing the chart.
options.risk: The botanical language could feel decorative; keep every leaf mark tied to a live value and keep the familiar dashboard structure unmistakable.

raised.raise: Keep sensor, forecast, and model metrics in fixed-width numeric columns.
Give the current reading and decision first-screen prominence; do not hide the live task below scroll.
Keep state transitions in the visible event log instead of letting them vanish.
Label the forecast horizon and burst duration in plain words and units.

options.label: Field Trial Sheet
options.thesis: A bold, practical record that makes each sensor reading and its watering consequence easy to compare.
options.viewport: A clean product header sits above one wide measurement-and-forecast chart, with the AI chain and diagnostics in a narrow left rail and the decision, pump state, and manual burst grouped on the right. A compact lower strip carries safety limits, model results, and simulated/live provenance.
options.risk: Its familiar agricultural-report logic is immediately legible, but it may feel less ownable than the field-guide direction.

options.label: Research Plate
options.thesis: A carefully composed research instrument with disciplined typography and visible registration details.
options.viewport: A clear top bar and left state rail frame the moisture chart as the central research plate; measured and forecast figures sit above it, with decision and pump controls in a standard right column.
options.case: The academic presentation context fits; the restrained plate language risks making live warnings and pump state too quiet.
options.risk: Registration detail must not compete with safety states or reduce projector contrast.

options.label: Garden Guide
options.thesis: A vivid plant-world palette makes the moisture state feel connected to the living subject.
options.viewport: A standard dashboard shell surrounds the trace and live readings; a bold chartreuse plant-state region ties the current probe value to the forecast, with ordinary decision and pump controls kept separate.
options.case: The plant and watering context resonate strongly; map-like organic fields can obscure the single sensor-to-pump chain.
options.risk: Keep the dashboard task obvious and avoid letting the map motif become navigation.

options.label: Data Sublime
options.thesis: High-density black-and-white marks turn live telemetry into a precise visual field.
options.case: It makes data unmistakable but sacrifices the color-coded state clarity needed in a live demonstration.
options.kept: Fixed-width numeric columns for stable, immediate comparison.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One signal owns the screen, with other details waiting one swipe away.
options.case: Strong focus cannot compensate for a layout that hides simultaneous system evidence.
options.kept: Make the current measurement the first thing the presenter sees.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: A sequence of sharply ruled coupons makes every state feel official and consequential.
options.case: Its sequential logic does not fit telemetry that updates continuously.
options.kept: Preserve state changes as a factual event history.

options.label: Movement Score
options.thesis: A precise timeline uses position, shape, and duration to encode change.
options.case: The notation is unfamiliar and would make a simple irrigation decision harder to read.
options.kept: Name the +15-minute forecast horizon and 40-second burst duration explicitly.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished, straightforward IoT analytics dashboard with conventional KPI cards and a line chart.
canonCard.viewport: A top navigation bar and compact KPI row lead into a large line chart, with a conventional control panel and compact model metrics.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar, but easy to mistake for a generic IoT starter dashboard.
